[b]ALAQAN NATIONAL ELECTIONS[/b]

Alaqar has, as of recent, undergone brief but significant political turmoil, having suffered a coup by an underground organization known as the Femboys Liberation Army with strong support from republican factions within the military and government. The government was replaced by the Femboys Council, a collection of FLA members, certain high ranking Alaqan officials, members of the military who had helped in the coup and influential public supporters of femboys, twinks and tomboys.

It was agreed upon that Alaqar would become a republic, the first republic of Alaqars entire existence. This decision marked a major departure from Alaqars traditional monarchical system and represents a new age for the Alaqan state. There was, however, a split in the council over how liberal or conservative the new constitution was to be. The constitution ended up being a moderate mix of capitalist principles with socialist elements as well as secular values, but two parties emerged out of the ashes of the conventions.

[b]Councils Coalition[/b]

Head: Rÿsul K. Huseyn
Focuses: Liberalism, Democratic Socialism, Pro-Neutrality, Strong Central Government, Environmental Protection

The Councils Coalition emerged from the conventions held in Shiganuur as the leftist leaning party, aiming for a stronger central federal government to ensure the countrys future was not divided. The Councils Coalition and its ideals are based around a neutral, liberal Alaqar with democratic and socialist elements implemented in the new twinkist society. The CC also hopes to create more national and state parks across the country and introduce social programs for Alaqan citizens. The Coalition, often referred to as the CC, is headed by Rÿsul K. Huseyn, a member of the Femboys Liberation Army that helped organize the takeover of the government. Rÿsul was selected as a level-headed but determined leader, seeing as he was not a radical femboy leader like Kovir or Astolfo. Rÿsul had chosen Niyaz Qodi as his running mate in the election to serve as Vice Kansler if elected.

[b]Alaqan National Party[/b]

Head: Aytolun Yosma
Focuses: Nationalism, Republicanism, Pro-Shamat, Strong States Rights, Militarism

The other party to arise out of the conventions was the Alaqan National Party. The Alaqan National Party, or ANP, brands itself on states rights, Alaqan nationalism and a strong political leaning on the ideas of Pan-Shamatism. The ANP desires to make Alaqar into a leading power within Shamat, strengthen Alaqars military capabilities and build a solid republic out of the way of peoples individual liberties. The Alaqan National Party is headed by Aytolun Yosma, an Alaqan military officer turned convention member and leader of the ANP. Yosma also participated in the coup and helped organize support from republican factions within the Alaqan military for the coup. Yosma is much more famous but also much more controversial than her main opponent, Huseyn. Yosma has chosen Parpilov Kovir as her running mate in the election to serve as Vice Kansler if elected.

[b]Dunmers Unitary Party[/b]

Head: Savumon Hlaur
Focuses: Dunmer Protection, Conservatism, Weak Central Government, Increased Dunmer Social Power

The Dunmers Unitary Party, also known humorously as the DUP, was formed in Giydiliac, Ulganmoor shortly after the creation of the new Alaqan constitution, and is a party based upon Dunmer rights and sovereignty. The Dunmer, otherwise known as dark elves, make up 35% of the Alaqan population and have lived in eastern Alaqar for thousands of years. Their ideals are based upon protecting the rights of the Dunmer living in Alaqar. The Dunmer were initially cautious of the new Alaqan regime when it took power in January, so the new republican government worked to relieve their concerns and worries quickly. There are still several problems left unresolved by both sides, however a fragile coexistence has lasted so far. The partys head, Savumon Hlaur, was elected by the delegates at the meeting in Ulganmoor. He is known for being the owner of Hlaur Oil Co., a solid sized oil refiner located mainly in the Dunmer provinces. Hlaur has chosen Midaendos Vinri as his running mate if elected.

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61579689][b]Intro[/b]
In the recent years a shocking and most disturbing trend has suffered in the nation of Rosenmarkke, which once a beacon of the liberal order and a champion of order and freedom, has seen itself destabilized and diminished both politically and internationally as the government seeks rapid centralism as an answer to a world of growing strife.

However, in their pursuit of centralism, the government has permitted many intolerable acts to occur within itself; namely: the increase of executive power, the cession of political control to the security administration, and the pursuit of popular narrative control amongst the citizenry. It is these three primary factors that have caused all other issues to appear.

Since the 1950s the nation of Rosenmarkke has degraded its legislature through various laws and agencies, removing the incentive to check the government by making it nigh impossible to properly regulate the states motions within and without. This is no more apparent than in the rise of the guardian state under the SCSID which is legally empowered to coup the state in order to maintain order, which while noble in practice, exhibits the danger of the SCSID turning against the government repeatedly as it did in 2005 and most recently in 2027. 

The prevailing power of the SCSID also allows it to influence the executive with the threat of a removal from power, thereby making the security system the executive and dimming the ability of the citizens and legislative to influence or place into power non-SCSID aligned figures.

This thusly turns the role of the citizen and the state in reverse, where it is now the state that can influence the citizen and the citizen is unable to hold them accountable, for fear of reprisal. In this manner the state can now feed the citizen what the citizen wishes to hear while slowly pulling the rug from beneath their feet, allowing the government to control the narrative.

This has occurred in the years of recent, with 2027-28 seeing the sudden explosion in the national media of the cult of Strømm, a clear attempt by the government to prop up a coup and hide the true nature of the plans of the regime, these being total control in the triumvirate and the sidelining of the legislative (shown further by the sudden downsizing of the old legislature from 300 or so to 150 members).

As a result of these alleged reforms for streamlining the government, the government failed to account for its aging armed forces and the security of Rosenmarkke itself, instead, placing itself in a position with its external grandstanding (which was merely propaganda to allow regime supporters to support external aggression and posturing), to be shaken into submission by foreign powers.

Thus is the rub of our tragic tale, for as of recently the Rosenmarkket navy now lies burnt out in dock, and its major military infrastructure unusable for anything but scrap metal. The recent war with Wuloosya and the Hochdeutsche has seen Rosenmarkket projection capabilities severely impacted, threatening the narrative of the great revolution, and the state itself. Furthermore with the SCSID leadership decapitated in their bunkers the engine of the state has been now removed, leaving only the people and the emergency mechanisms which now are scrambling to restore order in the face of a laughing world.

But, contrary to the pessimistic predictions of the various states that surround Rosenmarkke, namely those her enemy, the Elsyr Defense Union, there still exists a way out for by which I shall argue henceforth in the following papers. This being, the restoration of the historical union with our northern neighbor Montfleur.

Now one might perhaps give pause to such an idea, the consequences alone would disrupt the global economic order, where Montfleur has remained neutral for nearly a century and has interacted minimally with the external world beyond basic trade, Rosenmarkke has expanded its reach internationally, and is the head and member of several international organisations including the Thýven Hydronia Pact andThe Corridor Treaty Organisation. However, when one moves out the shock factor, they realise that such a union would be mutually beneficial if set up correctly, and even a restoration of the right order. 

It is thus with these reasons that I am in support of the unity of Montfleur and Rosenmarkke, for from it true peace on eastern Elseyr can be established.

- James Mjrkanlwyth (President of the International Association for the Reunification of Rosenmarkke and Montfleur)

[b]On the Economic Issues Facing Re-Unification[/b]
  In the opening note to these papers, President Mjrkanlwyth proposed a bold idea for the potential reunification of Montfleur and Rosenmarkke; however, such a reunification would prove difficult for a variety of reasons. Aside from the clear cultural and political divergences among the regions of the states involved, there is also a significant economic disparity that has arisen in Rosenmarkke and Montfleur. First, financial development has differed greatly in Rosenmarkke than in Montfleur due to Montfleur undergoing the massive decolonisation efforts it had to pursue under the government from 1930 to 1980. Second, Montfleur, under its policy of neutrality, has maintained lower economic inflows from investors and international companies than the more technocratic Rosenmarkke. Third, as a result of the prior two reasons, the financial situation between citizens in Rosenmarkke and in Montfleur has leaned more in favor of Rosenmarkke due to the progressive tendencies of its government in ensuring civilian welfare is maintained at the highest standard, whereas the Montfleurois government has done little, or has been unable to do much, for its own citizens, 18.4% of who, live below the poverty line. 

[i]Financial Development[/i]
As aforementioned, economic development between Rosenmarkke and Montfleur has differed greatly. Whereas Rosenmarkke was able to open itself to the wider market under its semi-socialist welfare system, Montfleur has maintained a relatively closed market for international trade, reluctantly doing trade with the Socialist Internationale. 

As a result, capital inflows for Rosenmarkke are higher, thereby allowing the government of Rosenmarkke to place more emphasis on its welfare system (which is one of the broadest in its region), while also placing a national mandate for economic development via an organised system of private/public economic planning. 

On the opposite side, Montfleur holds a protectionist stance on its economy, which, while holding higher industrial capacity than Rosenmarkke, has failed to reap the benefits of such a large industry, focusing mainly on internal improvements and post-colonial reconstruction. Indeed, it can be argued that the programme of decolonisation, which ran from 1930 to 1980 under those who were called Les Optimistes. Severely damaged Montfleurois development as the government focused primarily on the liberal moral order of decolonisation without focusing on the economic aspects, getting rid of colonies and resources like gifts.

The programme of decolonisation hit Montfleurois industry hard in the late 90s when the state faced a mounting debt crisis on the international stage, failing to pay off the loans that it had taken out to build its industrial capacity to ensure no burden was placed directly upon the citizens, causing a nationwide collapse which saw unemployment and inflation skyrocket and remain at levels that hadnt been perceived until the mid 2010s.   Thus, the ideological basis of governance within Montfleur proved to be its downfall. 

[i]Neutrality[/i]
Another key difference and issue between the two states is the concept of international relations. While one would assume that neutrality would bring in investors and opportunities abroad, this is usually coupled with a government willing and open to permitting such matters to occur. Unfortunately, the government of Montfleur, in its conservativeness, feared that mass investment would ruin the character of the nation, and as a result, limited heavy investment in order to promote a form of autarky. However, once again, the economists and government of Montfleur underestimated the cost of attempted autarky, placing the country back developmentally 10-20 years. 

Whereas Rosenmarkke approached with great eagerness the concept of international relations, seeking to protect itself via trade and economic networks favorable to its government, it was in this plan that the Rosenmarkket economy experienced numerous boom cycles across the late 20th and early 21st centuries, only just now experiencing any significant downturn due to political turmoil. 

It is in this that we can say Rosenmarkke need not unify with Montfleur to stabilise itself; all it needs is to reaffirm to the investors that it can indeed continue and stabilise itself through the pursuit of economic externalism. 

[i]The Financial Situation on the Home Front[/i]

Due to the reasons listed above, the personal financial situation of a citizen in Montfleur versus that of a citizen of Rosenmarkke is a deeply divergent world, whereas the citizen of Rosenmarkke can enjoy high welfare spending and government services, which aid in the tax burden of the state. The citizens of Montfleur struggle to maintain themselves above the poverty line, if not even maintain themselves within the middle class, where the upper echelons of Montfleurois society are locked away due to inheritance, with most industrialist families inheriting properties and companies, thereby creating a hereditary oligarchy in some manner.

Furthermore, the average Rosenmarkket citizen, while suffering from a higher tax burden, enjoys a wider range of freedoms and privileges economically in terms of economic choice; one can go abroad easily, travel across the country in comfort, and move and do business in another region. Whereas the average Montfleurois citizen maintains in their life a limited view of their opportunities, with most not attending university or even secondary education. 

The outdated nature of Montfleurois society further prevents social mobility as prejudices and tensions between the social classes remain, even despite efforts by the left-wing parties in the nation for nearly 200 years to upset the status quo; they have only managed to succeed in popular electoral and political reforms rather than economic ones, primarily due to the moralist majority in the National Assembly of Montfleur. 

[i]Closing[/i]
It is in these reasons that we see major divergences which would prevent or potentially prevent a stable long-term reunification between the two states, whereas the burden of support would fall upon the Rosenmarkke government to maintain and uphold the government of Montfleur and its citizens, thereby potentially risking the economy of Rosenmarkke itself. There simply exist far too many economic divergences in lifestyle, approach, and political nature to justify the lengthy and expansive task of reunifying two nations that have held separate trajectories for centuries now.

  - Josef Alben (Professor of Economics at Vysjllá Technical Institute)

Three days after Faris had staged the purge, all the dissenters had been tried. Under the charges of high treason and conspiracy to murder the leader of Hydronia, they were sentenced to death. Evidence was fabricated, and in many instances those who were on trial confessed falsely to save their own lives while damning a few more. The primary evidence to the trials was the statement made by Omar ibn Abdullah, who was now nowhere to be found.

Gunshots rang out through the streets. Crowds eyed the executions, hatred in their gazes for those who came together to kill the man of the people. Blood ran down cold pavement sidewalks.

In groups of three, they were executed. The shootings began at noon, and continued through the setting of the sun.

Faris stood on the balcony of the presidential palace, overlooking the executions that were happening around him. It was vivid beyond vividity, and yet he felt he was asleep. He had to be dreaming. He nearly pinched himself to wake up from this vision.

By the end of the day, all of the traitors were executed. Faris rested in his office, not glad that this had taken place but now calmer knowing that his position was cemented. The traitors were those that had the highest capacity to oppose him, and now there were none; if there were any less he was certain that they would remain quiet now that he had set a new precedent.

With the last of the light he saw as the bodies were collected and hauled into one large truck with the top of the container removed so that there would be more space. There were bodies upon bodies, and limbs poked out from the mass propped up only by the limbs of others. He knew that the destination was an unmarked mass grave somewhere off in some unknown area. It did not please him, but it sent a message that he knew needed to be sent.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=

[pre]Mirror Rim[/pre]]

Late at night, Faris remained in his suit and tie, unable think about going to bed. He felt some undue fear grip his heart, and he felt himself unable to rest. Perhaps it was anxiety at watching the executions, or perhaps his conscience from murdering his own brother catching up to him, but it was something that needed to be suppressed. He left his office and turned left to use a small restroom; there were others that were larger, but this small restroom was closest and he knew himself in need of quick respite.

Faris kept the lights off. He turned on the sink and began to wet his face with cool water, which ran down to his neck and dried upon reaching his shirt. Faris looked slightly deeper into the mirror which he had only looked at in passing. The darkness made it difficult to distinguish any features while he stood at a normal distance. Even then, it appeared as though there was some sort of abnormality; it was not that he could not make out the details of his face due to the darkness, but rather that there was a black shroud covering him. It unsettled him deeply.

A crack appeared on the mirror. Faris took a step away; his mind was screaming at him to move, yet his body was paralyzed with fear. Now the black shroud had dissolved, and what he saw unnerved him more: it was his own face, sneering at him. He was certain that this was not the expression on his own.

Suddenly the mirror shattered outwards and an arm black as coal reached out to him and grabbed him by the neck. It tightened its grasp, intending to kill him, and Faris quickly reacted by reaching for the knife at his side and bringing it down on the limb, cutting himself free. The rest of the limb retreated, but three more appeared and shot forth towards him.

Faris jumped back, coughing and clawing the still tight hand away from his throat. A creature from the depths of hell began to crawl out. One hundred arms reached through the small opening, clawing at anything they could reach to pull themselves through.

[i]"Guards!"[/i] Faris staggered backwards. He overcame the paralysis of fear that had taken hold of him and turned to open the door. At the moment he turned the handle he heard the sound of that horrid creature stumble and fall onto the ground with its many limbs already starting to reorient it to chase after him. He did not wait to look back; Faris sprinted down the hall.

The creature was behind him, and galloped with many legs and arms. Its myriad voices called out to him, stumbling upon each other, some mocking him and others weeping and others yet babbling incoherently as children. On the corridors were hands and shadows of hands reaching out to him, some colored as coal or tar and others with varying levels of decay, many with missing flesh and raw muscle exposed and others stripped to the bones and sinews.

Faris could only keep running. He sprinted straight down the corridor, and he could hear the creature gaining on him. He turned right, intending to get to his office, and he could hear the demon go past the turn with its many limbs trying to grab at the carpeted floor and slipping under the inertia. He looked back and saw the hands of the creature pulling itself around the corner of the wall; the mass of flesh reared its ugly heads with faces that were vaguely familiar to him.

He was closing in on his office door. He knew that if he could just lock himself in there, the strong wooden door would block out the devil that chased him. There was enough distance between him and the creature for him to feel confident he could make it, and when he finally reached his office he slammed the large door behind him and locked it. There was a strong impact, and the walls shook with force. The doorknob rattled wildly and the pounding of many fists against the door filled the office room. Faris scrambled to his desk, where he kept a revolver; he had no time to make sure that it was fully loaded, but rather kept it pointed at the door.

The pounding ceased, and the cacophony of voices slowly quieted and fell silent. Faris believed that the creature had left him, when suddenly the sound of shattering glass pierced the air behind him as thousands of mirror shards fell broken upon the floor. Faris whipped around, and once more the entanglement of arms and flesh had appeared. He had locked himself in the room with the creature.

The devil charged him, and he aimed and fired twice in quick succession. It did not stop the hurling mass from coming down upon him, and in the final moments he squeezed his eyes tight and fired once more.

For a few seconds there was silence and blackness. He squeezed the trigger again and again only to be met with the soft click of the revolver each time. He opened his eyes.

There was nothing there.

There were the sounds of footsteps, and suddenly frantic knocking on the large wooden door. [i]"President Al-Mansoori! Is everything alright? We heard you call for us and run into here, and sounds of gunfire!"[/i]

The knocking against the door ceased for a moment as the handle tried to turn, and then the knocking resumed. Faris took a moment to analyze the situation: he was unharmed, and the devil that had tormented him was gone.

He went to open the door. [i]"I am alright. Please, leave me be."[/i]

The guards left. He looked back into his office and saw that the mirror was intact. However, he could feel the cuts on his own face from where the bathroom mirror shards had cut him, and he tasted the slightest hint of blood.

[/spoiler]
